correctness.rationale: The input is visibly unimodular and odd, hence mean-zero. Jacobi–Anger gives precisely four retained Fourier frequencies. Their squared-modulus autocorrelations are directly computed and Parseval gives a closed fourth-moment polynomial in J0,J1,J2. Exact rational alternating-series bounds at t=1 prove the polynomial strictly exceeds one, independently checked by executing verify_bessel.py from its included path. The sixth-order Taylor coefficient 5/576 was reconstructed and independently verified using exact rational polynomial arithmetic. This is an explicit existential counterexample, not an extrapolation from finite numerical samples.

originality.rationale: The full 2026 Poisson source gives symmetric L-three contraction and a nonzero-mean S-one higher-exponent obstruction; neither implies mean-zero S-three L-four noncontraction. The 2010 Riesz theorem uses a distinct one-sided multiplier. A published Poisson endpoint calculation concerns a different multiplier and family. Actual semantically targeted searches by equivalent input classes, Fourier cutoff, target exponent and Bessel moments found no dominating or exact prior. Unindexed equivalence remains possible.
residual_risks: An inaccessible or unindexed prior result might contain the same mean-zero symmetric-section example under a different description. Search failure is not novelty certification.

value.rationale: The September 2026 theorem obtains Poisson L-three contractivity by positive Abel combinations of L-three-contracting symmetric Fourier sections, while conjecturing a complex L-four endpoint. The new zero-mean S-three L-four obstruction proves that directly upgrading that entire section argument is impossible. Crucially the first norm excess appears only at sixth order after quadratic and quartic cancellations, giving a mathematically motivated and reproducible explanation for why lower-order endpoint tests are inconclusive. The result is a structural barrier, not merely a change of normalization or a small numerical improvement.
